title: Attention: tokens look back
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json, experiments/logs.

blocks.text: Every column now knows only its own word. Attention lets each position look back at the others, and take what it needs.
blocks.say: Every column now knows only its own word. Attention lets each position look back at the others, and take what it needs.

blocks.text: From the last position, this is where the model looks, averaged over all 14 heads and all 24 blocks. Most of the weight goes to the chat's markers, the tokens that say who is speaking. About a fifth goes to Emma's question.
blocks.say: From the last position, this is where the model looks, averaged over all fourteen heads and all twenty-four blocks. Most of the weight goes to the chat's markers, the tokens that say who is speaking. About a fifth goes to Emma's question.

blocks.text: But each head looks for something different. Block 24, head 2, puts 65 percent on Manchester. Block 16, head 0, is the head that looks hardest at battery: 9 percent. And block 12, head 13, rests all of its weight on the very first token, when it has nothing to add.
blocks.say: But each head looks for something different. Block twenty-four, head two, puts sixty-five percent on Manchester. Block sixteen, head zero, is the head that looks hardest at battery: nine percent. And block twelve, head thirteen, rests all of its weight on the very first token, when it has nothing to add.

blocks.text: There is one rule. A position may look back, never forward. Battery can see How many city e-bike, but not packs, or Manchester. When the model writes, the future does not exist yet, so it is masked out in training too.
blocks.say: There is one rule. A position may look back, never forward. Battery can see, how many city e-bike, but not packs, or Manchester. When the model writes, the future does not exist yet, so it is masked out in training too.

blocks.text: Fourteen heads, side by side, in each of 24 blocks. Each one mixes what it found into the column, and passes it up.
blocks.say: Fourteen heads, side by side, in each of twenty-four blocks. Each one mixes what it found into the column, and passes it up.
